_doc: TRUTH judge goldens (scripts/journeys/judge_goldens.py, REWRITE R-HARNESS S1c): answers known without the judges. A ruler fact is read by a judge-free pixel ruler from the stored film's exact scan lines (a run of one fixture color on one scan line, in exactly these frames; it must not show in the 6 frames either side). An expectation says what a judge must or must not report on that film. A judge that misses one fails the run and cannot be blessed; a ruler fact the film does not show is NO VERDICT. Add a fact only with its evidence (who proved it, how) in `why`.

facts.why: FRAME OWNER REFACTOR proved by hand (PIXEL-PERFECT/ROOT-CAUSE.md P10, FEAT DOGFOOD BUILD 4d9e624a, cmux24, 2x): in the Ctrl-Shift-L spring the growing pane's held content leaves the shell color (#FF00FF) in a band from x=1568 that grows to 1684 px, frames 161-188; frame 189 is the final-size host. R-HARNESS checked it on the stored copy with the ruler at 14:5xZ (2026-11-03).

FRAME OWNER REFACTOR proved this band by hand on FEAT DOGFOOD BUILD 1d8e759e (PIXEL-PERFECT/ROOT-CAUSE.md P9, film px-5fe33a3-120x2/px-keys-held-2-s1r-s1); P10 does not cover the held-key film of build 4d9e624a. On this film (4d9e624a) the frames come from the judge-free ruler on the stored copy (15:0xZ, 2026-11-03): with the key held, the K3 hold keeps the growing pane's content at its first-press size, so the shell color (#FF00FF) shows inside the pane on row 514 in frames 164-190, 195-241 and 417-542 (816-2321 px wide at the end); the first span starts at x=1568 in exactly frames 164-190. video_judge.py (S1a) flags every band frame as a defect, as 'divider not shown' (frames 164-190, 194-554). Its 'gap or overlap' check does not fire over the band (its one 'gap or overlap' finding is frames 543-544, after it), though it does on the single-press film: a known limit of that check, left for the pixel judge work. Checked again by an independent reader in review 2 of #33930.

VIDEO JUDGE (STATUS 8176): the divider is dragged left past its clamp, then right past it. The judge before the drag split (#32947) read the film as one motion and reported 28 false 'reverse'; the fixed judge splits it into one motion per drag and reports none.
VIDEO JUDGE (STATUS 8176): the same clamp case on a row divider: 34 false 'reverse' before the drag split, none after.

FRAME OWNER REFACTOR (agent pixel-perfect, 2026-11-03, PIXEL-PERFECT/ROOT-CAUSE.md P11, corrected the same day): in this film (FEAT DOGFOOD BUILD 4d9e624a, cmux22, 2x; the divider dragged 150 pt right in 1 s, then back fast) the page pane's right content edge is short of its rest end (x=2721 inclusive, ring 1 red) in every frame of the slow drag, 218-356 (2, 4 or 6 px; 16 px at 218), and in frame 513 of the fast drag back (1 px), and in no other frame; every pixel of the gap is shell class. Checked by the owner with a pixel ruler and with judge_pixel v7 (blob c22403233dd7): 'content edge off | p1 (page) hi on row@514 | 140 frames (218-356, 513)', row@1126 the same. R-HARNESS read the same rows from v7 on the stored copy (off_ranges '218-356,513'), and the judge-free ruler finds the shell run at x 2705-2721 of row 514 and 1126 in exactly frames 218-356.

FRAME OWNER REFACTOR (agent pixel-perfect, 2026-11-03, P11): the page pane's LEFT content edge is off its pane only in frames 513-515 (+12/+21/+46 px), the fast drag back, where the page lags its pane (the page-window check reports frame 513 too): REAL. Frames 211-358 of the slow drag are no left-edge defect: 214-356 are the divider's drag cue over the page's left rings (a design cue, 'a drag always lights the band'), 211-213 and 357-358 are 'not found'; v7 reports them as information only. So the row's off frames are exactly 513-515: a judge that reports the cue frames as off fails this fact.

FRAME OWNER REFACTOR (agent pixel-perfect, 2026-11-03, judge_pixel item 3a): a FALSE POSITIVE of judge_pixel v7 (c22403233dd7), which reports 'gap | p0 (tui) hi on row@845 | shell visible up to 14 px past rest' (frames 229, 231, 518, 519). Row y=845 is where the moving p1/p2 row divider crosses, so the extra shell beyond p0's right edge is the neighbour column's row gap, not p0's. R-HARNESS read the stored film: in those frames row 845 shows the shell from p0's right edge (x=1568) to the window's right edge (x=2722), which is the p1|p2 divider band; the right column's panes and that divider all start at x=785 pt (1570 px), 2 px past p0's edge, which is p0's gap at rest.

FRAME OWNER REFACTOR (agent pixel-perfect, 2026-11-03, judge_pixel item 3b): a FALSE POSITIVE of v7 (c22403233dd7), which reports 'divider off' for divider p1|p2 on col@1916, frames 507-511 and 513-520 (+10/+20 px). judge_pixel derives the shown divider from the middle of the two content edges beside it, so a content edge that lags or is off its pane moves the 'divider' while the cmux divider layer (drawn in the same transaction as the pane layout) is on time. R-HARNESS checked the stored film: every one of those frames has p1 hi or p2 lo content edge off or late in the same frame, which carries the defect. Pair C (FRAME OWNER, 2026-11-04): the film never shows the divider layer (its band shows the shell), so judge_pixel no longer derives a film divider (the middle of two content edges only restated them); the divider is judged from the trace, against the gap between the two panes it separates. This fact now holds on that trace row: the trace's divider is centred on its panes' gap in every sample, so the judge reports no divider defect on this film.

facts.why: FRAME OWNER REFACTOR (agent pixel-perfect, 2026-11-03, judge_pixel item 3c): a DUPLICATE in v7 (c22403233dd7). judge_pixel counts the shell inside a pane once per pane and line (the exact shell pixels in the pane's visible span on that line), but reports it on both side rows of that pane and line, so each such defect shows twice: here 'shell inside the pane' on p1 (page) lo and hi on row@514, 155 frames (211-213, 218-358, ...) each, with the same frames and px. R-HARNESS checked the 40 judge_pixel films: 263 lo/hi pairs report the same detail. The shell inside a pane is not a side's: it belongs on one row per pane and line, never on a side row.

FRAME OWNER REFACTOR (agent pixel-perfect, 2026-11-03, judge_pixel item 3d): FrameScheduler.deliver ticks its clients in Dictionary hash order, so in some films the debug.motion trace client and the layout client of one frame run in the other order, and judge_pixel's fixed clock (a frame at t shows the trace sample of t minus one refresh) is one sample off for the whole film. The owner saw the tab strip and the page window one frame late in every moving frame of the 1x held-key film, and lag 0 in the 2x film of the same journey. Film: FEAT DOGFOOD BUILD e0e34bd6 (tag chrome-parity-feat-d9ef49f8c40f-v1, built from feat d9ef49f8c40f), filmed by the FRAME OWNER with kit 0d2cf84acb9 on cmux22, round sweep-d9ef49f-120x1-20261103T201621Z-cmux22 (gallery folder sweep-d9ef49f-120x1-120x1). R-HARNESS read the stored film's edges against the trace at each offset (2026-11-04, /work/tmp/r-harness/3d/explore-red.txt): over the frames whose candidate samples differ, p0 (tui) hi is within 1 px of the trace in 23 of 24 at +1 and 9 of 24 at the fixed clock; the divider p0|p1 (the middle of its two content edges) in 8 of 8 at +1 and 5 of 8 at the fixed clock. So the clock is +1, and against it p0 hi has no lag.

R-HARNESS (2026-11-04, /work/tmp/r-harness/3d/explore-red.txt): p0 (tui) hi is within 1 px of the trace in 22 of 22 moving frames at the fixed clock, 10 of 22 at +1 and 8 of 22 at -1. The page p1 is held by the K3 hold (its content keeps its first-press size), so p1's edges and the divider beside it follow no offset; the terminal's edge sets the clock, and it is the fixed clock's.

Pair C (FRAME OWNER, 2026-11-04): the trace check 'divider rect not centred on its panes' gap' (|the divider rect's centre - the middle of the gap between the two panes it separates| >= 1 device px, from the trace only). Red case named by the owner: frame 181 of this film, where both content edges are on their panes and v7 reported 'divider off' +2.5 px. R-HARNESS read the trace (2026-11-04, /work/tmp/r-harness/3b-compare/divider_centre.py): during the close the gap between p0 (hi edge 1560-1567 device px) and p2 (lo edge 1578-1571) closes from 18 px to 4 px around a fixed middle (1569 px), while the divider rect keeps 6 px from p0's edge (centre 1561-1568): off by 1-13 px in samples 181-192 and centred in every other sample. A base build without S3 (no closing slot), so the two outer pane rects are its panes. The off spans of a trace row are samples.
